prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, which opened the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I keep B020 as the whole prize and I want to say why in terms of mechanism, since that is the standard I apply to every candidate. The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation is a transparent model: two Dirac cones coupled by a moire potential, a single dimensionless parameter, and a prediction that the Fermi velocity vanishes at a magic angle. In 2018 nature then showed correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle, in a carbon system where nobody expected them. The central structure, flat bands at the predicted twist, is quantitatively understood, and the phenomenology has been reproduced independently by many groups and carried to twisted multilayers and transition-metal dichalcogenides. That is what I mean by a mechanism that is both simple and general. Round 1 did not weaken this case. What it did was sharpen the honest limits of the claim: it is a prediction of band flattening plus a discovery of phases, not an explanation of the superconductivity, and the citation should say exactly that and nothing more. I do not move to B024 as my preferred whole prize, but I would now accept it without hesitation, and I explain below why my position on B020 is a matter of degree and not of principle.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I do not think they are resolved by round 1. First, maturity: eight years is short, and if the pairing mechanism turns out to be, say, purely phononic or purely electronic, the committee may later wish its citation had been worded differently. A phenomenological citation mitigates this but does not remove it. Second, attribution: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, is outside the three names, and so is the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theory of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, which found the same physics of strongly reduced velocity at small angles. Calling Jarillo-Herrero the group-leader proxy for the experiment is a defensible Academy convention but it is a convention, not a fact about who made the measurement. Third, I accept the argument from Kroll and Lindroth that B024 has the cleaner credit and the longer track record. If the committee decides that a prize must be mature and cleanly credited above everything else, B024 wins on those criteria and I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are a textbook measurement-driven advance with the cleanest two-name credit, independently reproduced at the 1e-18 level, and the lineage objection (2005, 2012) is real but not disqualifying.
responses.response: I accept that the credit is cleaner than mine and that independent reproduction is stronger than for any moire result. On lineage, your argument that the lattice concept is distinct from the comb and from single-ion control convinces me more than it did in round 1: the magic-wavelength condition is a specific idea that removes the atom-number versus shift trade-off, and neither the 2005 nor the 2012 citation contains it. My remaining question is the one I put to you earlier: what do we learn about nature, as opposed to what do we measure better. The honest answer today is that the discoveries enabled by the clocks, such as varying constants and dark-matter limits, are null results so far. That does not make B024 unprizeworthy, since a record-setting instrument that others have confirmed is a legitimate basis, but it is why I still put a prediction-and-discovery pair first and treat B024 as my first fallback. If the committee does want to recognise B024, I would ask that the citation be worded around the invention of magic-wavelength trapping and not around the redefinition of the second, which has not happened.

responses.point: The lattice clock is a clean idea with a quantifiable payoff, whose measurements can be confronted with atomic theory (magic wavelengths, blackbody shifts), and Ye's credit rests partly on record accuracy rather than the original idea.
responses.response: Your last point is the one I find most useful because it parallels my own difficulty with B020: in both cases the credited experimentalist is the person who made a good idea work convincingly, not the person who first wrote the idea down. I think that is acceptable for Ye and for Jarillo-Herrero alike, and I would like the committee to apply the same standard to both. I also take your remark that the agreement between independent clocks and atomic theory shows the understanding is real. I would say the same about the flat-band structure being reproduced by scanning probes and transport in many groups. Where I am still not persuaded is that this makes B024 clearly the better whole prize, rather than an equally defensible one; the two ballots fail different tests, B024 on novelty of principle and B020 on maturity and Cao.

responses.point: The citation should be worded around the flat-band prediction and the observed phases, not around an explanation of the superconductivity, and the experimental credit is a judgement about the group leader that the committee should state openly.
responses.response: I agree on the wording and I have rewritten the citation accordingly: it names a prediction and an experimental discovery of phases, and it makes no claim about pairing. On Jarillo-Herrero as proxy for Cao, I do not think the committee can resolve this from the shortlist alone, and I would rather record it as an acknowledged limitation than pretend it is clean. Your question about B051 is fair and I now answer it directly. The hexatic story is not universal: hard disks melt first-order, so a citation would have to separate what is established for colloidal and defect-mediated systems from what is system-dependent. I do not think I can write that citation with confidence, which is a main reason I moved my own first-ranked ballot out of the preferred configuration.

responses.point: A citation can name the achievement without claiming nobody else contributed, youth alone is not disqualifying because the phases have been reproduced in several platforms, but the junior-researcher problem needs a clear justification; B024 is the better-documented fallback.
responses.response: I think your formulation is correct and I adopt it: the citation names the achievement, and the record of earlier band-structure work and of Cao's role should be stated in the committee's own background document. Where I would go further than you is on the fallback. If the committee cannot give a clear justification for the Cao omission, you say B024 is better documented, and I would follow that logic rather than defend B020 against the evidence. So our shared position is conditional: B020 if the committee is satisfied that the three names are a defensible reading of the original prediction and discovery, B024 otherwise. I would ask you what evidence, short of a historian's report, would settle the credit question for you, since I cannot find it in the shortlist material.

responses.point: B024 plus B019 gives two distinct experimental breakthroughs with three laureates, though Halzen alone is a fragile credit and the configuration should shrink to B024 alone if that credit cannot be defended.
responses.response: I appreciate that you would drop B019 rather than add names you cannot support, which I agree is the honest course. For my own part I do not think a two-part prize is the right way to resolve the disagreement between B024 and B020: the two parts would be an atomic-metrology achievement and an astrophysical discovery, whose only connection is that both are experimental. I also share your concern about the diffuse flux: most of the sources remain unidentified, which makes the discovery claim less settled than the flat-band case, though more settled than a single event. If the committee asks me which of your two configurations I could accept, it is B024 alone, not the pair.

responses.point: A two-part prize pairing a precision instrument with a genuine discovery about the cosmos is balanced and defensible, provided Halzen alone can be credited for IceCube, which is the weakest point.
responses.response: I take your balance argument seriously, and your own admission that B019 collapses if the credit cannot be defended is the key. In this shortlist I cannot see a supportable way to credit a collaboration-scale discovery to one person: the IceCube result is an experimental effort by hundreds of people, and the three-person room you mention does not by itself tell us who the other names should be. For that reason, and not because I doubt the discovery, I cannot support B019 as a second part. On your comment about my B051, I accept the criticism that the central claim is system-dependent; I would not now ask the committee to rank it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the origin of the superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene to be unresolved in a way that makes a prize premature, or whether a phenomenological citation is enough.
How to justify the omission of Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theorists under the three-name limit, which I cannot resolve from the shortlist record.
Whether lattice clocks demonstrate a new principle beyond a record-setting measurement, and whether the committee wants to wait for the redefinition of the second.
The hexatic phase story (B051) is cited from memory; I have not checked the experimental history, and its status relative to the 2016 prize remains unclear to me.
Whether a recusal ruling for Johansson on B042 is needed, which would not change my own configuration but affects how the discussion of alternatives is weighed.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict applies to B020, B024 or B051: I have no recorded collaboration with any of the credited persons. I am in the Gothenburg physics environment together with Eva Olsson and Goran Johansson at Chalmers, which is institutional proximity and not a collaboration. I note the conflicts disclosed by others in round 1 (Johansson on B042, Kroll's distant link to the Hall-Ye lineage for B024) and do not think either affects the B020 versus B024 question, but I would support the chair recording them. No new disclosure from my side since round 1.
